cues.en: Hi.
cues.zh: 嗨。

cues.en: I'm Ross, and I enjoy video games, or a lot of them.
cues.zh: 我叫Ross，我很喜欢电子游戏，或者说很多游戏。

cues.en: I also enjoy owning things.
cues.zh: 我也喜欢拥有东西。

cues.en: You know, like things in my hand or my immediate vicinity that I use frequently.
cues.zh: 你知道，就是手里或身边常用的那些东西。

cues.en: When I walk down the street, like I how people don't usually run up to me and try to take the clothes off my back, because it's generally understood by society that those are mine and belong to me. But see, just by me saying those things, we already have a problem.
cues.zh: 走在街上，人们通常不会冲过来扒我身上的衣服，因为社会普遍认可那些是我的、属于我。但你瞧，光是我这么说，就已经有问题了。

cues.en: Yeah. You can probably see where this is going.
cues.zh: 是的，你们大概能猜到接下来要说什么了。

cues.en: The video game industry has a lot of problems, like a lot of problems.
cues.zh: 电子游戏行业存在很多问题，确实是很多问题。

cues.en: I think regulators have no idea actually.
cues.zh: 我觉得监管机构其实根本不了解情况。

cues.en: But there's one problem in particular I've been hating for decades,
cues.zh: 但几十年来，有一个问题我尤为痛恨，

cues.en: and it's getting worse and worse.
cues.zh: 而且它还在愈演愈烈。

cues.en: And that is destroying video games so that no one can ever play them again.
cues.zh: 那就是彻底毁掉游戏，让任何人都再也玩不了。

cues.en: And I don't mean your brother sticking a disc in the microwave so that your copy is destroyed.
cues.zh: 我说的可不是你弟弟把光盘塞微波炉里，把你那张盘给报废了。

cues.en: I mean everyone's.
cues.zh: 我是说，大家的。

cues.en: There's a really specific way this happens.
cues.zh: 这件事发生的方式非常具体。

cues.en: Just as a quick refresher, for most of gaming history, this hasn't been much of an issue. Most games contain the code that interfaces with the hardware, and run the game, and that's the whole story. Now for online multiplayer games, it's a little different. Where a lot of the older ones will let players host the server that runs the game, then other people would connect to it, or sometimes give you the software to make that server a standalone thing, and connect to that. But over time, more and more companies decided, hey,
cues.zh: 简单回顾一下：在游戏史上的大部分时间里，这都不算什么大问题。大多数游戏都包含了与硬件交互、运行游戏的代码，事情就这么简单。现在，在线多人游戏的情况有些不同。很多早期的游戏会让玩家搭建运行游戏的服务器，其他人再连接过去；有时也会提供服务器软件，让你把服务器单独搭起来，再连接进去。但随着时间推移，越来越多的公司开始想：嘿，

cues.en: instead of letting the player host the game, what if we did it instead?
cues.zh: 要是不用玩家来搭建游戏服务器，改由我们来搭建呢？

cues.en: Well, there are pros and cons to that, but that can be a valid approach...
cues.zh: 这种做法确实各有利弊，但也算是一种可行方案……

cues.en: In theory.
cues.zh: 理论上来说。

cues.en: But here's the problem.
cues.zh: 但问题就在这儿了。

cues.en: The games industry has a horrible,
cues.zh: 游戏行业在维护自家老游戏方面的记录，

cues.en: horrible track record of maintaining its own games.
cues.zh: 可以说是差得一塌糊涂。

cues.en: There was a large study conducted last year that showed only 13%
cues.zh: 去年有一项大型研究表明，

cues.en: of published video games are still available by the publisher commercially.
cues.zh: 所有发行过的电子游戏中，发行商仍在商业上提供支持的只有区区 13%。

cues.en: So what happens when the publisher takes over the responsibility of running the game? Well, it's usually pretty good while they support the game. Then when they stop, it's a complete nightmare, and has been responsible for destroying more video games than any other practice.
cues.zh: 那么，把运营游戏的责任全交给发行商会怎样？在他们还愿意支持这游戏时，体验通常都还挺好；可一旦他们放弃支持，彻底的噩梦就来了——这种做法毁掉的电子游戏，比其他任何手段都要多。

cues.en: That's a big shift,
cues.zh: 这是个巨大的转变，

cues.en: because the industry is trying to get users to go from a model where they get to keep their game, regardless of when support ends,
cues.zh: 因为业界正试图让用户从“无论支持何时结束都能保留游戏”的模式，

cues.en: to one where the game dies forever.
cues.zh: 转向“游戏永久消亡”的模式。

cues.en: I'm not a fan. For companies that do this,
cues.zh: 我不赞成。对于这样做的公司，

cues.en: the number of games that survive in any form, forget being available commercially,
cues.zh: 能以任何形式存活的游戏数量——更别提商业上可获得的——

cues.en: is a lot worse than 13%.
cues.zh: 比 13% 要糟糕得多。

cues.en: I did an informal investigation on it a few years ago, and found it was closer to 3%.
cues.zh: 几年前我做过一次非正式调查，发现更接近 3%。

cues.en: I think that number may have gotten even lower since I did that.
cues.zh: 我觉得自从我做了那之后，这个数字可能还更低了。

cues.en: From my perspective, this has felt like a slow moving coup to take away ownership from more and more people over time.
cues.zh: 在我看来，这感觉就像一场缓慢推进的政变，随着时间推移，一点点剥夺越来越多人的所有权。

cues.en: So video game publishers are making billions
cues.zh: 所以电子游戏发行商赚得盆满钵满

cues.en: selling you a game as a good,
cues.zh: 把游戏当作商品卖给你，

cues.en: not telling you how long it will last,
cues.zh: 却不告诉你它能撑多久，

cues.en: purposefully killing it later so you're left with nothing, but then they get to keep your money.
cues.zh: 之后故意把它弄死，让你手里什么都不剩，但他们却能把你的钱留下。

cues.en: Now don't confuse this with rentals.
cues.zh: 别把这个和租赁混为一谈。

cues.en: Rentals are sold as a service,
cues.zh: 租赁服务会告诉你，

cues.en: and tell you exactly how long they last.
cues.zh: 租来的东西确切能用多久。

cues.en: A customer who rents something is informed.
cues.zh: 租东西的顾客会被告知这一点。

cues.en: Video game publishers don't want that,
cues.zh: 电子游戏发行商可不想这样，

cues.en: because they know if they put on the box exactly
cues.zh: 因为他们知道，要是在包装盒上明确写出

cues.en: how long the game will last, then that will hurt sales a lot.
cues.zh: 游戏能玩多久，销量就会大受影响。

cues.en: So it's important to withhold that information from the customer,
cues.zh: 所以，不能把这个信息告诉顾客，这很重要，

cues.en: because customers are used to video games lasting
cues.zh: 因为顾客已经习惯了电子游戏几乎能玩

cues.en: forever more or less.
cues.zh: 一辈子。

cues.en: You could have bought games from the seventies that still work today.
cues.zh: 你买的七十年代游戏，到今天可能还能玩。

cues.en: You could have bought games from the nineties with online multiplayer that connect to the Internet that still work today.
cues.zh: 你在 90 年代买的那些带联网多人模式的游戏，连上互联网后现在依然能玩。

cues.en: Even if the companies that made them no longer exist.
cues.zh: 哪怕制作它们的公司早就倒闭了。

cues.en: But a lot of publishers like to place modern video games that are designed to die, but they won't tell you when,
cues.zh: 但很多发行商却喜欢把那些注定会停服、却又不说明何时停服的现代游戏，

cues.en: right alongside ones that last forever, so they can try to cash in on customer confusion.
cues.zh: 直接和能永久运行的游戏摆在一起卖，借此利用消费者的信息差来捞钱。

cues.en: Because the average person believes they are buying something.
cues.zh: 因为普通人总觉得自己是在买一件属于自己的东西。

cues.en: Now I personally hate this practice because art has innate value to me.
cues.zh: 就我个人而言，我讨厌这种做法，因为艺术对我有内在价值。

cues.en: And while it's debatable if video games are art,
cues.zh: 虽然电子游戏算不算艺术还有争议，

cues.en: they undeniably
cues.zh: 但它们无可否认地

cues.en: contain
cues.zh: 包含

cues.en: art.
cues.zh: 艺术。

cues.en: So seeing games destroyed to me, is the same as if someone were to walk into an art museum and start torching the paintings.
cues.zh: 所以在我看来，看到游戏被毁掉，就像有人走进美术馆开始焚烧画作一样。

cues.en: And it's insult to injury that companies that do this face no penalties.
cues.zh: 更让人雪上加霜的是，这么做的公司不受任何惩罚。

cues.en: Nor is there a good reason for them doing it. I won't get into the details here, and you may hear excuses as to why companies have to destroy your games,
cues.zh: 他们这么做也没有正当理由。我这里不细讲，你可能会听到一些借口，解释公司为何必须毁掉你的游戏，

cues.en: even though they largely didn't used to do that,
cues.zh: 尽管他们以前基本上不这么做，

cues.en: even for online multiplayer.
cues.zh: 即使是网络多人游戏也不这么做。

cues.en: But what I found is that the people saying that tend to either be uninformed,
cues.zh: 但我发现，那些这么说的人要么不了解情况，

cues.en: or else incredibly
cues.zh: 要么特别

cues.en: unimaginative,
cues.zh: 缺乏想象力，

cues.en: and can only see things one way.
cues.zh: 只能从一个角度看问题。

cues.en: When we order the pancakes, they're gonna bring the maple syrup. The maple syrup is supposed to be on the table before the pancakes.
cues.zh: 我们点了松饼，他们就会把枫糖浆端来。枫糖浆本来应该在松饼上桌前就放在桌上的。

cues.en: Course when they bring the maple syrup after the pancakes it'll definitely be too late.
cues.zh: 当然，等松饼上桌后才把枫糖浆端来，那肯定就太晚了。

cues.en: How is that gonna be too late, Right? Yeah.
cues.zh: 这怎么会太晚呢？对吧？是啊。

cues.en: Talking with people who defend this practice can feel a lot like that.
cues.zh: 和那些为这种做法辩护的人交谈，感觉也差不多。

cues.en: I'm reminded of when Microsoft was sued by the Department of Justice for bundling Internet Explorer with Windows, and Microsoft claimed it was impossible
cues.zh: 这让我想起微软曾因将 Internet Explorer 与 Windows 捆绑销售而被美国司法部起诉。微软当时声称，根本不可能

cues.en: to separate it from Windows 98,
cues.zh: 把它从 Windows 98 中分离出来，

cues.en: even though it wasn't even with Windows 95 when it launched, and through the power of hindsight they actually did remove it from Windows years later. So it was possible earlier,
cues.zh: 可 Windows 95 刚推出时，它甚至都没捆绑 Internet Explorer。多年后回头看，微软确实把它从 Windows 中移除了。所以，以前能做到，

cues.en: it's possible in the future,
cues.zh: 将来也能做到，

cues.en: but it's impossible right now because the company has spent a lot of time trying to make it difficult.
cues.zh: 只是现在不行，因为公司花了很多时间让这件事变得困难。

cues.en: That is such a good analogy for what is happening with games. You have no idea.
cues.zh: 这个比喻太贴切了，游戏界的现状就是如此，你根本想象不到。

cues.en: Anyway, no matter how you look at it, this is such an obvious assault on consumer rights.
cues.zh: 无论怎么看，这都是对消费者权益赤裸裸的侵犯。

cues.en: And in any other industry, a company destroying what they sold you would be illegal.
cues.zh: 换作其他任何行业，公司亲手销毁卖给你的东西都是违法的。

cues.en: If only there was something we could do about this.
cues.zh: 要是我们能做点什么就好了。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 其实，

cues.en: as it so happens, we have the best opportunity
cues.zh: 巧的是，我们正好迎来了

cues.en: ever to take action on this. A few months ago, the company Ubisoft announced it was shutting down a game of this nature called The Crew. Now The Crew, I think is a flawed but remarkable game, but none of that matters here. What matters is it had at least 12,000,000
cues.zh: 采取行动的绝佳机会。几个月前，育碧宣布将关停旗下的一款同类游戏《The Crew》。在我看来，《The Crew》虽有瑕疵但也算得上优秀，不过这都不重要。重要的是它拥有至少 1200 万

cues.en: players,
cues.zh: 玩家，

cues.en: so this affects a lot of people. And Ubisoft is headquartered in France,
cues.zh: 波及面非常广。而且育碧的总部位于法国，

cues.en: And France has some of the strongest consumer laws in the world.
cues.zh: 而法国拥有世界上最严格的消费者权益保护法。

cues.en: See, this isn't really about the crew, or even Ubisoft.
cues.zh: 你看，这其实跟开发团队无关，甚至跟育碧也无关。

cues.en: It's about trying to find a weak link in the industry, so governments can examine this practice to stop publishers from destroying our games.
cues.zh: 关键在于找到行业的薄弱环节，让政府能审查这种做法，阻止发行商毁掉我们的游戏。

cues.en: Outside of The United States,
cues.zh: 在美国以外，

cues.en: this practice is very hazy legally.
cues.zh: 这种做法在法律上非常模糊。

cues.en: Many governments don't even have laws regarding this.
cues.zh: 很多政府甚至根本没有相关法律。

cues.en: I'm not kidding. More on that later.
cues.zh: 我没开玩笑，后面细说。

cues.en: If we can find even one major country to penalize this practice,
cues.zh: 只要能找到一个主要国家来惩处这种做法，

cues.en: that might fix everything.
cues.zh: 也许就能解决一切。

cues.en: Because the thing about letting you keep your game is it's not that expensive for companies to do it, especially if it's a known requirement from the beginning, then it's almost negligible.
cues.zh: 因为让玩家保留游戏这件事，对公司来说成本并不高；尤其如果从一开始这就是已知要求，那成本几乎可以忽略不计。

cues.en: So if a company knows they have to let you keep your game in one country, they may as well make it global policy because then they've already done the work.
cues.zh: 所以，如果一家公司知道在某个国家必须让玩家保留游戏，那它不妨把这变成全球政策，因为相关工作反正已经做了。

cues.en: It really could take just one victory to end this.
cues.zh: 真的可能只需要一次胜利就能终结这一切。

cues.en: So even if you have no interest in the crew, if you just wanna keep your games,
cues.zh: 所以，即使你对 The Crew 毫无兴趣，只要你只是想保留自己的游戏，

cues.en: keep watching. There's more. Hearing about this shutdown has caused me to go on a research odyssey,
cues.zh: 就继续看下去。还有更多内容。听到这次停服的消息后，我踏上了一场研究之旅，

cues.en: to see if I could find any possible way to get governments to examine the legality of destroying your games.
cues.zh: 想看看能否找到任何可能的办法，让政府审查“销毁你的游戏”的合法性。

cues.en: I have been waiting for an opportunity like this.
cues.zh: 我一直在等这样的机会。

cues.en: This problem has been going on for decades,
cues.zh: 这个问题已经持续了几十年，

cues.en: but it usually only affects a small minority of players that are too dispersed to do much. Most have moved on when a game is killed, and the industry has been counting on that lethargy. So an event like this that's big enough to do something is like the planet's aligning.
cues.zh: 但通常只有少数玩家会受到影响，而且他们分散各处，很难有所作为。游戏停服后，大多数人就不再关注了，而行业一直在利用这种惰性。所以，像这样足以推动改变的大事件，简直就像行星连珠。

cues.en: We have to take action on it. Now I do not think I'm the ideal person to do this.
cues.zh: 我们得采取行动。我不觉得自己是做这件事的最佳人选。

cues.en: I'm not a legal expert.
cues.zh: 我不是法律专家。

cues.en: I have limited reach.
cues.zh: 我的影响力也很有限。

cues.en: Honestly, everything about what I've been doing has been an amateur effort.
cues.zh: 说实话，我所做的一切都只是业余水平。

cues.en: I don't even want to be doing this.
cues.zh: 我甚至根本不想干这事。

cues.en: But if you care about this issue, I'm what you're stuck with, because nobody else has stepped up.
cues.zh: 但如果你在乎这个问题，你也只能指望我了，因为没有别人站出来。

cues.en: And I guess there is one thing that makes me a good candidate for this, and that at least with me, you're getting maximum hustle.
cues.zh: 不过我觉得有件事让我成了合适的人选，那就是至少在我这儿，你会看到全力以赴的拼劲。

cues.en: I have decades worth of resentment on this issue.
cues.zh: 在这个问题上，我已经积攒了几十年的怨念。

cues.en: You know when a dog is eating and somebody yanks away its food bowl, even nice dogs will get angry or even attack you? That's how I feel about the industry on this.
cues.zh: 你知道狗在吃东西时，如果有人猛地拽走它的食盆，就算是温顺的狗也会发怒甚至攻击你吗？我对这个行业在这件事上的感受就是这样。

cues.en: Since I started this campaign, I've spent hundreds of hours on it, talked to multiple lawyers,
cues.zh: 自从发起这项行动以来，我已经投入了数百个小时，跟多位律师谈过，

cues.en: worked with over a 100 volunteers,
cues.zh: 与100多名志愿者合作，

cues.en: sent hundreds and hundreds of emails,
cues.zh: 发了成百上千封邮件，

cues.en: trying to chase down every single lead I can find.
cues.zh: 努力追查我能找到的每一条线索。

cues.en: I have been relentless on this.
cues.zh: 我在这件事上一直毫不松懈。

cues.en: I've felt it too.
cues.zh: 我也有同感。

cues.en: In the game trailer for Yes, Your Grace, the king is hearing so many requests from his subjects that at one point he just keels over from it all. Yeah. That's exactly what it feels like.
cues.zh: 在《Yes, Your Grace》的游戏预告片里，国王听着臣民们没完没了的请求，最后直接不堪重负倒下了。没错，就是那种感觉。

cues.en: And after months of research...
cues.zh: 经过数月的研究……

cues.en: Yes. I have found ways we can do something.
cues.zh: 是的。我找到了可以采取行动的办法。

cues.en: Not just long shots either, but really viable routes.
cues.zh: 不只是希望渺茫的尝试，而是真正可行的路线。

cues.en: I have found what I think are all the agencies worldwide
cues.zh: 我找到了我认为全球范围内

cues.en: best equipped to take action on this issue. I've also found dead ends.
cues.zh: 最有能力就这个问题采取行动的所有机构。我也找到了一些死胡同。

cues.en: A lot of dead ends.
cues.zh: 碰了很多壁。

cues.en: In fact, I found so many that if I had known earlier what I know now, I could have saved myself at least a month's worth of work.
cues.zh: 其实我碰到的壁太多了。要是早点知道现在知道的这些，至少能省下一个月的工夫。

cues.en: Like I said, this is an amateur effort, so I'm trying to make up for that with even more hustle.
cues.zh: 就像我说的，这是业余之作，所以我正努力加倍拼劲来弥补。

cues.en: And because I'm treating this like it's my only shot, because it probably is, I'm not stopping at the crew.
cues.zh: 我把这当成唯一的机会，因为很可能真的是，所以我不会止步于组建团队。

cues.en: Remember, the crew is just a means to an end, which is to stop companies from destroying your games.
cues.zh: 记住，团队只是达成目标的手段，目标是阻止公司毁掉你的游戏。

cues.en: So rather than just getting the government to interpret the law, I figure why not go to the source while we're at it. So in addition to the consumer action, we're also pursuing government petitions.
cues.zh: 所以与其只是让政府去解释法律，我想不如顺水推舟，直接从源头下手，因此除了消费者维权行动，我们还在发起政府请愿。

cues.en: Now hold on, I know what some of you are thinking. These are not normal petitions,
cues.zh: 先等等，我知道你们有些人在想什么，这可不是那种普通的请愿，

cues.en: where you get a bunch of people to sign to show that people care and hope companies do the right thing.
cues.zh: 拉上一帮人签名来表达诉求，然后寄希望于企业自觉做好事。

cues.en: Come on guys. Give me more credit than that.
cues.zh: 拜托，各位，别把我想得那么天真。

cues.en: No. These are government initiatives,
cues.zh: 不，这些是政府主导的举措，

cues.en: where if we pass a certain threshold,
cues.zh: 一旦我们越过某个门槛，

cues.en: the government has to respond. It's the law. And for some of them, are almost guaranteed
cues.zh: 政府就必须回应。这是法律规定。而且其中一些几乎 guaranteed

cues.en: to be debated.
cues.zh: 会被辩论。

cues.en: Yeah. We'll see. But this is how a lot of laws get made.
cues.zh: 是啊。我们走着瞧。但很多法律就是这么制定的。

cues.en: So what's in these petitions?
cues.zh: 那这些请愿书里都写了什么？

cues.en: Well, it varies for every country since they all have different rules, but they all share the same fundamentals.
cues.zh: 各国情况不同，因为规则各异，但基本要素是共通的。

cues.en: I tried to design the fairest proposals I could that still solve the problem.
cues.zh: 我尽量设计了最公平、同时又能解决问题的方案。

cues.en: Yet remember that naysayers, I'm trying to solve
cues.zh: 但请唱反调的人记住，我是在试图解决

cues.en: the problem.
cues.zh: 这个问题。

cues.en: But I'm also trying to keep the scope as narrow as possible.
cues.zh: 但我也在尽量把范围缩到最小。

cues.en: I am not trying to reform the games industry.
cues.zh: 我并不是想去整顿整个游戏行业。

cues.en: I am just trying to stop companies from destroying games that they've sold to you. That's it.
cues.zh: 我只是想阻止公司销毁那些已经卖给你的游戏。仅此而已。

cues.en: So with that in mind,
cues.zh: 所以基于这一点，

cues.en: while the game is being supported,
cues.zh: 只要游戏还在维护期内，

cues.en: any game, absolutely nothing would happen. Companies could do whatever they wanted. We're going for a light touch. It's only when support ends that requirements will kick in. The first is any game sold,
cues.zh: 任何游戏，都不会受到任何影响。游戏公司想怎么搞就怎么搞。我们采取的是轻度监管。只有在停止支持时，这些要求才会生效。第一条是，任何出售的游戏，

cues.en: or licensed for those of you who wanna be pedantic,
cues.zh: 或者咬文嚼字点说，任何获得许可的游戏，

cues.en: will be required to be left in a functional state when support ends.
cues.zh: 在停止支持时，都必须保持在可用状态。

cues.en: This does not mean a 100% perfect state, but it means a hell of a lot better than completely inoperable.
cues.zh: 这不代表游戏得处于百分之百完美的状态，但总得比彻底玩不了好得多。

cues.en: It would also require no connection to the publisher or affiliated parties in order for it to continue functioning.
cues.zh: 而且，游戏要能继续运行，就不能依赖连接发行商或其关联方。

cues.en: So it would need to be patched to either be offline,
cues.zh: 所以它得打上补丁，让它可以离线运行，

cues.en: or have private hosting only. It's the only way. Anything less, and the game dies.
cues.zh: 或者只能通过私人服务器托管。没有别的办法。做不到这些，游戏就会消亡。

cues.en: And yes, this would include DRM that needs to connect to the internet.
cues.zh: 没错，这也包括那些需要联网的 DRM。

cues.en: And because I'm being forced to go to all this trouble, I really wanna end this. So this would also apply to games with microtransactions.
cues.zh: 既然我都被迫费这么大劲了，我是真想把它彻底解决。所以这也适用于包含微交易的游戏。

cues.en: Except we didn't say microtransactions,
cues.zh: 不过我们没直接用“微交易”这个词，

cues.en: since these were in plain English. So this would cover free to play games, because if you've been sold something like a virtual horse,
cues.zh: 因为提案用的是通俗易懂的大白话。所以这也会涵盖免费游戏，因为如果你花钱买了一匹虚拟马，

cues.en: but then the publisher destroys the game, well now you can't access your horse.
cues.zh: 结果发行商把游戏给关了，那你现在就骑不了你的马了。

cues.en: I've been told undisturbed
cues.zh: 有人告诉我，“平静占有权”

cues.en: possession is a term for what I'm talking about here. And finally, these rules cannot be superseded by end user license agreements,
cues.zh: 就是我在这里所表达的意思。最后，这些规则不能被最终用户许可协议覆盖，

cues.en: since that's how companies have been getting away with highway robbery in the first place, especially in The US.
cues.zh: 因为各大公司本来就是靠这玩意儿来明抢的，尤其是在美国。

cues.en: There's no point in having rights if you have to sign them away just to play a game.
cues.zh: 如果必须签字放弃权利才能玩游戏，那拥有这些权利就毫无意义。

cues.en: I'm sure a few of you right now are scoffing at this proposal, but just remember Internet Explorer, guys. It was impossible.
cues.zh: 我相信在座有些人正在嘲笑这个提议，但别忘了 Internet Explorer，各位。那曾是不可能的。

cues.en: And that's it, pretty much.
cues.zh: 差不多就是这样。

cues.en: Now one thing we left off the table, but it's kind of an open secret we'd be willing to compromise on, or at least I would, would be if a company doesn't fix the game, but they give you all the information,
cues.zh: 有一件事我们没摆上台面，但这是个公开的秘密，我们愿意妥协，至少我愿意——那就是如果公司不修复游戏，但把所有信息、

cues.en: tools,
cues.zh: 工具、

cues.en: software, and so on, so that a programmer could be reasonably expected to get it working again.
cues.zh: 软件等等都给你，让程序员有理由能让它重新运行起来。

cues.en: Yeah. That's an acceptable substitute.
cues.zh: 是的，这是个可以接受的替代方案。

cues.en: Though the resentment some others had helping on this was strong, and they didn't trust companies not to abuse a provision like that. And they could be right, so we left it out of the proposals.
cues.zh: 不过，有些人对协助这件事心存强烈不满，他们不信任公司不会滥用这样的条款。他们可能是对的，所以我们没把它写进提案里。

cues.en: We also left out this applying to all software and restricted it just to video games.
cues.zh: 我们也没让它适用于所有软件，而是仅限电子游戏。

cues.en: Now don't get me wrong. I personally think all commercial software should have these provisions also.
cues.zh: 别误会，我个人认为所有商业软件也都应该有这些条款。

cues.en: But this is already such an uphill battle that expanding the scope would invite many more enemies and weaken our odds.
cues.zh: 但这本来就已经是一场艰难的战斗了，扩大范围只会招来更多敌人，让我们的胜算变小。

cues.en: Remember, I am single issue.
cues.zh: 记住，我只关注一个议题。

cues.en: The point is, even if you don't own the crew, you'll still be able to do something if you live in one of the countries where these petitions were launched.
cues.zh: 关键是，即使你不拥有这艘船，只要住在发起这些请愿的国家之一，你仍然能做点什么。

cues.en: This is a multi pronged attack.
cues.zh: 这是一场多管齐下的行动。

cues.en: I have prongs for everyone.
cues.zh: 我给每个人都准备了一招。

cues.en: Well, no, but a lot of people.
cues.zh: 好吧，也不是所有人，但很多人。

cues.en: It's complicated.
cues.zh: 这事挺复杂的。

cues.en: Remember a while back when there were so many versions of Watch Dogs for sale that somebody made a spreadsheet on how to buy the game? It's not that bad, but it does have a lot of variables.
cues.zh: 还记得前阵子《看门狗》（Watch Dogs）版本多到有人专门做了张表格，来教大家怎么买游戏吗？现在虽没那么夸张，但变数确实不少。

cues.en: What I've found is that what people can do varies on where they live, and whether they own the crew or not. But even then, it can still be confusing.
cues.zh: 我发现大家能采取的办法因居住地而异，也取决于是否拥有《飙酷车神》（The Crew）。即便如此，整个情况依然让人摸不着头脑。

cues.en: So I've seen it as a priority to make this as easy as possible for everyone.
cues.zh: 所以我觉得当务之急，就是尽可能让所有人都能轻松搞定。

cues.en: To that end, I've been working with volunteers to launch a website to do just that.
cues.zh: 为此，我一直在和志愿者合作推出一个网站，专门做这件事。

cues.en: Stopkillinggames.com.
cues.zh: Stopkillinggames.com。

cues.en: I hope you can remember that name.
cues.zh: 希望大家能记住这个名字。

cues.en: It has the two g's there back to back that might throw some people off.
cues.zh: 里面有两个连着的 g，可能会让一些人看花眼。

cues.en: It's a multilingual website that can easily steer you exactly where you need to go to have maximum impact. Some people can do multiple things, so I even tried to prioritize their options a little bit. In fact, you can even just stop watching and go here if you want. There's nothing else you have to know that's not on the site. We have blazed a trail for you to hit back against the industry. All you have to do is follow it. We've done all the hard parts for you.
cues.zh: 这是一个多语言网站，能轻松把你引导到最能发挥作用的地方。有些人能同时做几件事，所以我甚至试着把他们的选项稍微排了个优先级。其实，你甚至可以直接关掉视频，现在就打开这个网站。网站上已经包含了所有你需要知道的东西。我们已经为你铺好了反击游戏行业的道路，你只需要跟着走就行。难的部分我们都替你搞定了。

cues.en: See, people can complain about the games industry,
cues.zh: 你看，大家可以抱怨游戏行业，

cues.en: but the reality is all internet comments are meaningless.
cues.zh: 但现实是，网上的评论都毫无意义。

cues.en: None of your comments matter,
cues.zh: 你的评论都无关紧要，

cues.en: unless a government official is reading them. That's what this is.
cues.zh: 除非有政府官员在看。这就是现在的情况。

cues.en: In fact, if you've gotten lost by anything I've said, here's all you need to remember. File complaints if you can, sign petitions if you can, get others to do one and two. And you can do that at stopkillinggames.com.
cues.zh: 其实，如果你没听懂我刚才说的内容，只要记住这一点就行：能投诉就投诉，能签请愿书就签，也让其他人做这两件事。你可以去 stopkillinggames.com。

cues.en: That's it. That's everything. You can tune everything else out like some sort of zen master if you know those three things. But maybe you think I'm exaggerating what we can do. Well, why don't you judge for yourself?
cues.zh: 就这些，这就是全部。如果你掌握了这三点，就能像禅师一样屏蔽其他一切。不过，你可能觉得我夸大了我们的能力。不如你自己来判断？

cues.en: Since no one else has stepped up on this issue, I'm assuming command to play general on this attack.
cues.zh: 既然没人愿意站出来处理这件事，那我就接手指挥，负责这次进攻。

cues.en: So, you wanna see my battle plans?
cues.zh: 想看看我的作战计划吗？

cues.en: I'll show you my battle plans.
cues.zh: 我给你看看我的作战计划。

cues.en: This could take a little while.
cues.zh: 这可能要花点时间。

cues.en: Okay, future Ross here. Some bad news. Like I said, this is an amateur effort, so even though some of these petitions were submitted weeks ago,
cues.zh: 好吧，未来的 Ross 插播一下。有个坏消息。就像我之前说的，这只是业余搞搞，所以即便有些请愿几周前就提交了，

cues.en: recording, we're still waiting on all of them to open up for signing. So here I am making a hype video to go send everybody to the right place, and they're still not ready yet. They haven't been rejected,
cues.zh: 在录制视频时，我们仍然在等它们全部开放签署。所以我这边正做着宣传视频打算把大家都引流过去，结果它们还没准备好。倒是没被驳回，

cues.en: we're just waiting on governments.
cues.zh: 只是在等官方审批。

cues.en: So this is kind of a nightmare for me. Oh well. We're moving forward anyway.
cues.zh: 所以对我来说简直是场噩梦。好吧，管他呢，我们继续往前推进。

cues.en: We do have links to where they're going to show up though, so that's something.
cues.zh: 不过我们确实有它们之后会展示在哪里的链接，这也算挺不错了。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Battle plans.
cues.zh: 作战计划。

cues.en: Now before we get into regions, the first option is worldwide,
cues.zh: 在我们开始讲区域之前，第一个选项是全球。

cues.en: and it's eligible for literally anyone who owned the crew.
cues.zh: 任何拥有过《飙酷车神》（The Crew）的人都完全符合资格。

cues.en: Yeah, anyone.
cues.zh: 是的，任何人都可以。

cues.en: Aren't you glad I cleared up those dead ends?
cues.zh: 我把那些走不通的路都理清了，你们是不是很高兴？

cues.en: Although it does have a critical flaw that can't be avoided.
cues.zh: 不过它确实有一个无法避免的致命缺陷。

cues.en: See, the option for all owners of the game is to contact the DGCCRF,
cues.zh: 你看，游戏所有者的选择就是联系DGCCRF，

cues.en: France's National Consumer Protection Agency. You go through this website here. They accept complaints worldwide,
cues.zh: 法国国家消费者保护局。你可以访问这个网站，他们接受来自世界各地的投诉，

cues.en: but there is a catch. The catch is they want everyone to contact Ubisoft
cues.zh: 但有个问题，问题在于他们想让大家都去联系 Ubisoft

cues.en: first.
cues.zh: 首先。

cues.en: So that means everyone is going to have to contact Ubisoft support,
cues.zh: 也就是说，每个人都得先联系 Ubisoft 客服，

cues.en: tell them to fix the game,
cues.zh: 让他们修好游戏，

cues.en: then when Ubisoft refuses,
cues.zh: 然后等 Ubisoft 拒绝，

cues.en: or two weeks have passed,
cues.zh: 或者等两周过去，

cues.en: then you can contact France.
cues.zh: 你才能联系法国那边。

cues.en: This is a major setback, because gamers are not known for their long attention spans.
cues.zh: 这是个重大挫折，因为玩家可不以注意力持久著称。

cues.en: So asking people to wait up to two weeks before taking a second step may ruin us. I may be asking the impossible here. I don't know. This right here could be exactly why the games industry has been able to get away with this crap for so long, because no one has the attention span for this second step. Some of you can do it though. I know it. Some of you. But let's look at the rest of the campaign, because I am not stopping there. God, no. Though remember, everything I'm about to show you can be done in addition to that worldwide step. So there's no one or the other here. And with that, let's start with the outskirts,
cues.zh: 所以，让人等上两周才走第二步，可能会毁了我们。我可能是在要求不可能的事。我不知道。这很可能正是游戏行业能长期逃避这种破事的原因，因为没人有耐心走第二步。不过你们有些人能做到。我知道。你们有些人可以。但让我们看看这场运动的其余部分，因为我不会止步于此。天哪，不会。不过记住，我接下来要展示的一切，都可以在那一步全球行动之外额外去做。所以这不是二选一。那么，我们就从外围开始，

cues.en: Australia.
cues.zh: 澳大利亚。

cues.en: Okay. Australia has a two pronged attack.
cues.zh: 好。澳大利亚有两招。

cues.en: First, if you own the crew, you can file complaints to the ACCC,
cues.zh: 首先，如果你拥有 Crew，可以向澳大利亚竞争与消费者委员会（ACCC）投诉，

cues.en: and they may do something. There was news not long ago about the ACCC going after the games industry.
cues.zh: 他们或许会采取行动。前不久有新闻说，ACCC 要对游戏行业采取行动。

cues.en: For god's sake, we need to find a way to piggyback onto this. Don't go after them and ignore customer games being destroyed.
cues.zh: 看在老天的份上，我们得想办法借这个势。别只盯着他们，却不管玩家的游戏被毁。

cues.en: Don't do that to me, Australia. But besides that, Australia is also the first of our government petitions.
cues.zh: 澳大利亚，别这样对我。不过除此之外，澳大利亚也是我们第一个发起政府请愿的地方。

cues.en: And anyone in Australia can sign these, not just owners of the crew. And honestly, you guys need to hurry up, because once it's approved, we only have a four week window.
cues.zh: 而且澳洲的任何人都能签署，不限于是 Crew 的所有者。说实话，大家得抓紧了，因为一旦获批，我们只有四周的时间窗口。

cues.en: Except of course it's not ready yet, even though it's been submitted. They give us a small window, but then don't tell us when it starts.
cues.zh: 当然，虽然已经提交了，但现在还没准备好。他们给的窗口期很短，却又不告诉我们具体何时开始。

cues.en: Oh my god. Now the upside is we only need 50 Australians to sign, but that's nothing. If we show up with 50, they may not take it seriously.
cues.zh: 天呐。不过好消息是，我们只需要 50 个澳洲人签名，但这根本不算什么。如果我们只拿着 50 个签名去，他们可能根本不会当回事。

cues.en: I'd rather we showed up with 50,000.
cues.zh: 我倒希望我们能凑到5万人。

cues.en: It's like a wise game ad once said, There's no kill like overkill.
cues.zh: 就像某个明智的游戏广告说的，没有什么比过度杀伤更致命。

cues.en: This is the most time sensitive element of the entire operation.
cues.zh: 这是整个行动中最时间敏感的环节。

cues.en: Go sign it as soon as you can.
cues.zh: 尽快去签吧。

cues.en: Future Ross again. I just got word from the Australian government that the petition looks fine, but they can't open it for signing until April 22, or maybe May 15. They don't know. So they can't even meet the four week deadline they're holding us to. What the hell, Australia?
cues.zh: 又是我，未来的Ross。我刚收到澳大利亚政府的消息，说请愿书看起来没问题，但他们要到4月22日，或者可能是5月15日才能开放签名。他们自己也不确定。所以他们连自己给我们定的四周截止期限都达不到。搞什么啊，澳大利亚？

cues.en: Moving on over, next we have Brazil.
cues.zh: 接下来，我们看看巴西。

cues.en: Now Brazil is the wild card in all of this. All the feedback I received said their consumer protection agency would probably be ineffective,
cues.zh: 巴西是整件事里最大的变数。我收到的所有反馈都说，他们的消费者保护机构大概指望不上，

cues.en: but having a class action lawsuit
cues.zh: 但发起集体诉讼

cues.en: very likely would work.
cues.zh: 很可能会奏效。

cues.en: Apparently the argument of we sold you a product but we can take it back at any time, doesn't fly with a lot of judges down there. Now at the time of this video, the situation was still in limbo, so this one may or may not happen.
cues.zh: 显然，“我们把产品卖给你，但随时能收回”这种说法，在当地很多法官面前根本站不住脚。制作本视频时，情况仍悬而未决，所以这场诉讼还不一定会发生。

cues.en: If it does happen, however, the cost of a class action lawsuit could be affordable if we have a fundraiser.
cues.zh: 不过真要发生的话，要是我们办一场募捐，集体诉讼的费用或许负担得起。

cues.en: I was told to 4 figure some estimate.
cues.zh: 他们让我估算一个四位数的金额。

cues.en: I currently do not have plans for a fundraiser, but if this looks viable, yeah, we may do one later. Don't worry. 90% of the battle plans still work even if no one spends a dime.
cues.zh: 我目前还没打算办募捐，但如果看起来可行，之后可能会办。别担心，就算一分钱都不花，90% 的作战计划依然行得通。

cues.en: Brazil is just part of the attack on all fronts mentality I've been taking. Moving on up is The United States.
cues.zh: 巴西只是我采取的全面出击策略的一部分。接下来要往上推进的地方是美国。

cues.en: Okay,
cues.zh: 好的，

cues.en: and moving on is Canada.
cues.zh: 接下来是加拿大。

cues.en: Now the thing about Canada is the federal agencies can't do much on this issue, so we have to look at the provinces.
cues.zh: 加拿大的情况是，联邦机构在这件事上起不到太大作用，所以我们得把目光转向各省。

cues.en: Okay okay, The United States.
cues.zh: 好了好了，聊聊美国。

cues.en: Listen guys, I wanna keep it real with you. The US is the suicide mission of this operation.
cues.zh: 大家听我说，我想跟你们说句掏心窝的话：把美国当突破口简直就是自杀任务。

cues.en: Unlike a lot of other countries, the laws are not gray on this issue, and at this point in time it's almost hopeless.
cues.zh: 和其他许多国家不同，美国在这方面的法律毫无灰色地带，眼下基本可以说是毫无希望了。

cues.en: Almost.
cues.zh: 只能说“基本”吧。

cues.en: Owners of the crew can still contact the FTC,
cues.zh: 《The Crew》的玩家依然可以联系 FTC（美国联邦贸易委员会），

cues.en: and I've been given coach points by a lawyer we can tell them to increase our odds to look into this. I am still not expecting a victory here. It's more like I just wanna be sure our options are truly dead in The United States before I write it off. I don't wanna pronounce the patient dead too quickly. You know how that goes. And hey, don't forget. If you own the crew, you still have that option to contact France directly.
cues.zh: 有位律师给我提供了一些沟通要点，我们可以这样向他们反映，来提高介入调查的几率。但我依然不抱太大获胜的希望。更确切地说，我只是想彻底确认在美国真的无路可走，然后再彻底放弃。我不想过早宣告病人死亡，你们懂我的意思。对了，别忘了，如果你拥有《The Crew》，你依然可以直接联系法国方面。

cues.en: In fact, I prefer you do that before you contact the FTC, since it has way better odds.
cues.zh: 其实，我更希望你联系FTC之前就这么做，因为成功率会高得多。

cues.en: Now if you're an American and don't own the crew, which is probably the majority of my audience,
cues.zh: 如果你是美国人，又没有游戏所有权，而这可能是我观众中的大多数，

cues.en: then I have nothing for you. I'm sorry guys, I really tried.
cues.zh: 那我就帮不了你了。抱歉各位，我真的尽力了。

cues.en: I just couldn't find anything.
cues.zh: 我就是找不到任何办法。

cues.en: Game ownership really is as bad as the naysayers say in The United States. The best I can do is tell you to get the attention of someone else who does qualify to do something. Remember the three points:
cues.zh: 在美国，游戏所有权确实和反对者说的一样糟糕。我最多只能建议你去引起其他符合条件的人的注意，让他们采取行动。记住这三点：

cues.en: If you're an American and don't own the game, you're number three.
cues.zh: 如果你是美国人，又没有游戏所有权，那你就是第三种情况。

cues.en: All right, back up to Canada, and ding ding ding, Canada has our second petition to government.
cues.zh: 好，回到加拿大，叮叮叮，加拿大是我们的第二份请愿书提交对象。

cues.en: So if you are a citizen or resident, head on over and sign it. We only need 500 for government to respond.
cues.zh: 如果你是加拿大公民或居民，快去签名。我们只需要 500 个签名，政府就会作出回应。

cues.en: But again, let's try to get a lot more than that, Now
cues.zh: 不过，还是尽量多争取一些签名。现在

cues.en: for owners of the crew, we didn't check every last one, but the provincial consumer protection agencies look pretty dire. I cannot endorse going through them at this time. It's almost certainly gonna be better if you just sign the petition. Crossing the ocean again, we have The UK.
cues.zh: 对于船员的所有者，我们没有逐一核实，但各省的消费者保护机构看起来情况不太乐观。我目前不建议通过这些机构处理。几乎可以肯定，直接签请愿书会更好。再一次跨越海洋，我们来到了英国。

cues.en: And it's a similar story as Canada. The consumer protection options look hopeless.
cues.zh: 情况和加拿大类似，消费者保护方面的选择看起来都没希望了。

cues.en: But hey, we have a government petition.
cues.zh: 不过，我们还有一份政府请愿书。

cues.en: If we get 10,000 signatures,
cues.zh: 如果能征集到 10,000 个签名，

cues.en: government will respond.
cues.zh: 政府就会作出回应。

cues.en: And if we get a 100,000,
cues.zh: 如果能征集到 100,000 个签名，

cues.en: then it's considered for debate in parliament.
cues.zh: 议会就会考虑将其列入辩论议程。

cues.en: Now those sound like big numbers, because they are, but we have six months to get them. So I think if I keep campaigning, we can do this.
cues.zh: 这些数字听起来很大，因为确实不小，但我们有六个月时间来达成目标。所以我想，只要我继续推动，我们就能做到。

cues.en: And we move inland to the main attack here. First let's stop by Germany.
cues.zh: 接下来我们转向内陆，来到这次行动的主战场。先去德国看看。

cues.en: Germany is one of the few EU countries where their national consumer protection is powerful enough to act on this, despite Ubisoft being a French company.
cues.zh: 德国是少数几个国家消协足够给力、能对此采取行动的欧盟国家之一，哪怕育碧是一家法国公司。

cues.en: So this is one of the few exceptions where you should contact the local agency first,
cues.zh: 所以这是少数几个你应该先联系当地机构的例外情况，

cues.en: then contact France, like everyone else. Now I learned late in the process, Germany and France have the option to petition their governments also.
cues.zh: 然后再像其他人一样去联系法国。后来在这个过程中我才了解到，德国和法国还可以向各自政府请愿。

cues.en: However, their thresholds are kind of high, and I can't hope to cross them without making serious inroads with foreign YouTubers,
cues.zh: 不过他们的门槛都挺高的，要是不能先在外国 YouTuber

cues.en: or other media sources first.
cues.zh: 或其他媒体渠道那里取得实质性突破，我就别指望能达标了。

cues.en: So if we get enough support and publicity,
cues.zh: 所以如果我们获得足够的支持和宣传，

cues.en: sure, we can add German and French petitions to the list. But not today. And that brings us to the heart of this: France.
cues.zh: 当然，我们可以把德语和法语的请愿书也加入列表。但不是今天。这就引出了核心：法国。

cues.en: This is where our most powerful attacks are.
cues.zh: 这里是我们最强大的攻势所在。

cues.en: French owners of the crew are the space marines of this operation.
cues.zh: 团队中的法国业主就是这次行动的海军陆战队。

cues.en: You have more options than anyone.
cues.zh: 你们的选择比任何人都多。

cues.en: The more you can do, the better. In fact, most people's best option is probably your weakest.
cues.zh: 能做得越多越好。事实上，大多数人最好的选择可能恰恰是你们最弱的那个。

cues.en: Besides the DG CCRF,
cues.zh: 除了DG CCRF，

cues.en: we'll also be sending registered mail to Ubisoft as part of summoning a government mediator
cues.zh: 我们还会向Ubisoft发送挂号信，作为请政府调解员介入的一部分，

cues.en: to take legal action on the customer's behalf.
cues.zh: 代表客户采取法律行动。

cues.en: It's almost like having your own prosecutor.
cues.zh: 这几乎就像拥有了自己的检察官。

cues.en: Amazing.
cues.zh: 太棒了。

cues.en: And just to hit every last stop, French citizens will be contacting the UFC Couchoisie,
cues.zh: 最后一步，法国公民将联系UFC Que Choisir，

cues.en: a powerful consumer advocacy group with a great record of defending gamer rights. And we actually juiced the whole process in France a little earlier prior to April, but that was the special operations phase of things. That part's over now, so don't worry about it. And for the rest of the European Union, this is where most of our dead ends were, since first I thought people should contact their consumer protection agencies.
cues.zh: 这是一个强大的消费者权益倡导组织，在维护玩家权益方面有着出色的记录。其实我们在四月之前就在法国提前推进了整个流程，但那属于特殊行动阶段。那个阶段现在已经结束了，所以不用担心。至于欧盟其他国家，这正是我们大多数死胡同所在的地方，因为起初我以为人们应该联系他们的消费者保护机构。

cues.en: By and large, no. They tend to only look at national businesses, and Ubisoft is in France.
cues.zh: 总体来说，不行。他们通常只处理本国企业，而育碧在法国。

cues.en: So then the documentation says to contact the European consumer center,
cues.zh: 所以，文档上说要联系欧洲消费者中心，

cues.en: and no, I don't advise that either. We did do that for a while, but the answers were all over the place.
cues.zh: 不过我也不建议这么做。我们之前试过一阵子，但得到的答复五花八门。

cues.en: Some said Ubisoft could do whatever they wanted because of the license agreement, Others said Ubisoft was liable to provide the service forever, which is kind of insane. I mean that's going farther than even I want.
cues.zh: 有人说，育碧可以根据许可协议为所欲为；也有人说，育碧有义务永久提供这项服务，这就有点离谱了。我是说，这甚至超出了我的预期。

cues.en: But most of them had no idea how to handle this. One clerk said they had never heard of someone make this kind of complaint before.
cues.zh: 但他们大多数人根本不知道该怎么处理。一位工作人员说，以前从没听过有人提这种投诉。

cues.en: Another one of them said it is unclear if these actions from the company are legally permitted.
cues.zh: 另一位则表示，还不清楚公司的这些做法在法律上是否被允许。

cues.en: There is no clear legal regulation for this.
cues.zh: 对此目前还没有明确的法律规定。

cues.en: So that's from the European Union itself, guys. There's no consistency.
cues.zh: 伙计们，这可是欧盟官方的原话。完全缺乏一致性。

cues.en: Nobody knows what the hell is going on. There's apparently no laws on this.
cues.zh: 根本没人搞得清楚到底是怎么回事。显然这方面还没有任何法律约束。

cues.en: What year is this?
cues.zh: 今年是哪一年？

cues.en: I mean, we're still getting robbed.
cues.zh: 我是说，我们还是在被抢劫。

cues.en: It's amazing game companies have been able to go on for so long exist between the cracks in the wall like this, like cockroaches.
cues.zh: 游戏公司能这样在墙缝里生存这么久，像蟑螂一样，真是惊人。

cues.en: We need to shine light on it.
cues.zh: 我们需要把这件事曝光。

cues.en: And on that note, the final lane of attack is the moonshot,
cues.zh: 说到这个，最后一条进攻路线是登月计划，

cues.en: which is the European Citizens Initiative.
cues.zh: 也就是欧洲公民倡议。

cues.en: It's like the other petitions but way bigger.
cues.zh: 它和其他请愿差不多，但规模大得多。

cues.en: This one is ambitious.
cues.zh: 这个很有野心。

cues.en: It might actually be delusional for me to attempt this. I don't know yet. But we would need 1,000,000
cues.zh: 我尝试这个可能确实是不切实际。我还不知道。但我们需要一百万

cues.en: signatures
cues.zh: 个签名

cues.en: across the entire European Union for this one. And there are some caveats,
cues.zh: 整个欧盟范围内，一百万个。而且还有一些附加条件，

cues.en: so in reality, more than a million. However, we will have one year to get these. I sure as hell can't get this from my audience alone, but that's a lot of time. If I campaign hard enough, maybe we can get those. And if that wasn't enough, this is also the weakest part of the campaign. Because while we're ready to go, it takes months for the EU to approve your proposal before signing. So that means there's going to be months delay between now and when this goes public.
cues.zh: 所以实际上要超过一百万。不过，我们有一年时间来收集。光靠我的观众肯定搞不定，但时间很充裕。如果我足够努力地宣传，也许能拿到。而且这还不算完，这也是整个行动中最薄弱的一环。因为虽然我们准备好了，但欧盟批准你的提案需要好几个月才能开始签名。所以从现在到正式公开之间会有好几个月的延迟。

cues.en: That is the kiss of death. That means we'll lose most of the momentum from April, and I'll have to come out and campaign for this again months from now. This one may be a bridge too far, I don't know. But again, this is me attacking on all fronts.
cues.zh: 那简直是死亡之吻。这意味着我们会失去四月积攒的大部分势头，几个月后我还得再次公开出面为此拉票。这一项可能迈得太远了，我也说不准。但还是那句话，这是我全线进攻。

cues.en: And that's the campaign.
cues.zh: 这就是这场竞选。

cues.en: We have up to 11 fronts of attack,
cues.zh: 我们最多有 11 条进攻战线，

cues.en: with maybe 13,
cues.zh: 也许 13 条，

cues.en: though in reality three of these are pretty iffy.
cues.zh: 但实际上其中三条相当悬。

cues.en: But the rest are relatively solid. This is happening, guys. This strategy is my absolute best effort as an amateur.
cues.zh: 其余的相对稳固。各位，这事正在发生。作为业余选手，这套策略已经是我全力以赴的极限。

cues.en: Now I'm biased when I say this, but if you care about not losing your games in the future,
cues.zh: 我这么说可能有点偏心，但如果你在意将来还能玩到这些游戏，

cues.en: this is the best chance you're ever gonna get to do something about it. As far as I know, no one has ever challenged the legality of game destruction,
cues.zh: 这是你唯一一次、也是最好的机会，能为此做点什么。据我所知，从来没人质疑过销毁游戏是否合法，

cues.en: and certainly no one's attempted it on this scale.
cues.zh: 更没人试过以这种规模来做。

cues.en: And I can't say by how much,
cues.zh: 至于规模会扩大多少，我说不准，

cues.en: but this is gonna get bigger too.
cues.zh: 但这件事肯定还会扩大。

cues.en: In fact, the next phase after this is to essentially spam myself on the internet to try to get more attention on this.
cues.zh: 事实上，接下来的阶段就是在网上到处宣传自己，争取让更多人关注这件事。

cues.en: I'll do interviews,
cues.zh: 我会去接受采访、

cues.en: appearances,
cues.zh: 公开露面、

cues.en: just try to get people to make Twitter posts, whatever.
cues.zh: 尽力发动大家发 Twitter，怎么都行。

cues.en: I don't really want to do that, but if that's what it takes to end this, I'll do it. I have a giant list of people I plan to contact, though you don't have to wait. If you have an audience and want me to talk about this, you can save me the trouble and contact me directly.
cues.zh: 我其实不太想这么做，但如果只有这样才能解决问题，我愿意配合。我列了一长串打算联系的人选名单，不过大家也不用干等着。如果你有受众平台，希望我来聊聊这件事，不妨直接联系我，也省得我到处去找人了。

cues.en: Or you can skip me entirely.
cues.zh: 或者你完全可以绕过我。

cues.en: I don't have to be involved in this. Just send people to stopkillinggames.com.
cues.zh: 这事儿不需要我参与。直接把大家引导到 stopkillinggames.com 就行。

cues.en: It'll take care of the rest.
cues.zh: 剩下的它来处理。

cues.en: I mean, it's a joke. I even have to do any of this for us to try not to get robbed.
cues.zh: 我是说，这就是个笑话。我甚至还得做这些，就为了让我们尽量不被抢。

cues.en: But that's gaming for you.
cues.zh: 但游戏业就是这样。

cues.en: One thing to keep in mind is the trajectory for gaming is so bad,
cues.zh: 要记住的一点是，游戏业的发展轨迹太糟了，

cues.en: we have absolutely nothing to lose.
cues.zh: 我们绝对没什么可失去的。

cues.en: I mean, how does gaming get worse than publishers destroying your games?
cues.zh: 我是说，游戏业还能比发行商毁掉你的游戏更糟吗？

cues.en: We've already had a glimpse of the future too.
cues.zh: 我们也已经瞥见过未来了。

cues.en: It's history now, but when Microsoft unveiled the original Xbox One, their plans showed us what game companies have in store for us. A surveillance device necessary to use the system that collects biometric data off you, you needing to connect to the company every twenty four hours or else you're locked out of your system, and when they eventually end support, your entire game collection becomes unplayable.
cues.zh: 现在这已成历史，但当年微软发布初代 Xbox One 时，他们的计划向我们展示了游戏公司为我们准备了什么。一个使用系统所必需的监控设备，会收集你的生物识别数据；你必须每二十四小时连接一次公司服务器，否则就会被锁在系统之外；而当他们最终结束支持时，你的整个游戏库都变得无法游玩。

cues.en: Welcome to the future.
cues.zh: 欢迎来到未来。

cues.en: Now soon afterwards they realized they came in too hot and had to walk some of that back, but the industry has been taking the boiling frog approach since.
cues.zh: 很快他们就意识到自己来得太猛，不得不往回收一部分，但整个行业从那以后一直在用温水煮青蛙的方式。

cues.en: This is where we're already headed if we don't do anything on this. Now I can't say if this campaign will be successful or not, but what I can say is if people put in the minimum effort, then we are going to get answers on this, and close the book on this one way or the other. Again, if we pass the petitions,
cues.zh: 如果我们对此什么都不做，这就是我们已经走向的方向。现在我不能说这场运动会不会成功，但我能说的是，如果人们付出最低限度的努力，那么我们就会在这方面得到答案，并以某种方式了结这件事。再说一次，如果我们通过请愿，

cues.en: governments
cues.zh: 政府

cues.en: have to respond and own that answer.
cues.zh: 就必须回应并承担那个答案。

cues.en: If consumer agencies get enough complaints,
cues.zh: 如果消费者机构收到足够多的投诉，

cues.en: they probably will too.
cues.zh: 它们可能也会采取行动。

cues.en: We won't have any more of this no clear regulation
cues.zh: 以后就不会再有这种监管不明的

cues.en: crap. I can almost promise you that much.
cues.zh: 破事了。我几乎可以保证。

cues.en: Plus, if we win, can you imagine how good it will feel in the future knowing all your games are safe
cues.zh: 再说，要是我们赢了，想想看，以后知道所有游戏都安全，

cues.en: and you only have to think about whether you like the game or not?
cues.zh: 你只需要考虑自己喜不喜欢这款游戏，该有多开心？

cues.en: That's my vision of gaming for the future.
cues.zh: 这就是我对未来游戏的愿景。

cues.en: It's a little different from the industry's.
cues.zh: 它和业界的愿景有点不同。

cues.en: And if we lose, we'll at least get told straight to our faces that in a democracy you can never own video games that you paid for, no matter how many people want that to happen.
cues.zh: 即使我们输了，至少也能听到一句当面的大实话：在民主制度下，花钱买的游戏你永远无法真正拥有，哪怕呼吁的人再多也没用。

cues.en: I guess this will be a civics lesson then.
cues.zh: 那我猜，这就算是一堂公民课了。

cues.en: Finally, I'd like to end this by saying thank you to Ubisoft. Oft. You're a French company and you pulled this crap.
cues.zh: 最后，我想向 Ubisoft 说声谢谢。呵，堂堂一家法国公司，居然能干出这种破事。

cues.en: And you did it to one of your flagship titles with millions of players.
cues.zh: 而且祸害的还是你们拥有数百万玩家的旗舰大作。

cues.en: If this had been Electronic Arts or Blizzard Activision, I would have had nearly the options that I do.
cues.zh: 如果这是Electronic Arts或Blizzard Activision，我几乎会有同样的选择。

cues.en: And a month later you made a PR statement of saying people should get comfortable not owning their games,
cues.zh: 一个月后你们发公关声明说，人们应该习惯不拥有自己的游戏，

cues.en: and then go on to lie in that same interview about online games being safe, as you're killing the crew. I mean, what are you gonna do next? Threaten the judge?
cues.zh: 然后还在同一次采访里谎称在线游戏是安全的，同时却在裁掉《The Crew》团队。我是说，你们接下来还要干什么？威胁法官吗？

cues.en: Here I've been thinking I have no way to fight this, and you go and create one of the best openings ever for me. Shame on me if I don't act on that.
cues.zh: 我一直在想自己没办法对抗这件事，结果你们却给我创造了有史以来最好的机会之一。如果我不抓住，那才是我自己的耻辱。

cues.en: I mean, it's not perfect, but this is a solid
cues.zh: 我知道它并不完美，但这是个难得的机会

cues.en: opportunity here.
cues.zh: 就在这里。

cues.en: If we can't win on this, we'll never win. There's no doubt in my mind.
cues.zh: 如果这件事我们都赢不了，那就永远赢不了。我对此毫不怀疑。

cues.en: You set yourself up for us, so we'll swing as hard as we can and see what happens.
cues.zh: 你给了我们这个机会，我们会全力以赴，看看结果如何。

cues.en: Alright. That's it. Go to stopkillinggames.com.
cues.zh: 好，就这样。去 stopkillinggames.com 看看。

cues.en: Don't forget about the European citizens initiative. It's coming in a few months.
cues.zh: 别忘了欧洲公民倡议，几个月后就要启动了。
